compatibility.instructions: Does this grain preserve all contracts: backup module is additive, no existing tool/route/ranking/migration altered, runbook and matrix delta are prose? Any changed behavior?

correctness.instructions: Is the drill correct: snapshot in stable id order, TRUNCATE CASCADE wipe, ID-preserving re-insert, per-table count plus id-set verification, invalid snapshots fail closed with the corpus intact? Do the PGlite tests and the real-PG test prove round-trip identity including stable flow URIs?

evidence.instructions: Is evidence sufficient: new drill tests green on PGlite and real PostgreSQL locally, db non-PG suite green, python/hygiene/validators green, Graft green, CI db-foundation job wired for exact-head proof? Any drill claim without execution?

reliability.instructions: Any nondeterminism or resource risk: is snapshot order stable, are restores idempotent-safe (re-running restore without wipe would conflict — documented scratch-only?), are invalid inputs rejected before any write?

scope.instructions: Anything beyond the corpus-subgraph drill plus runbook: per-item takedown automation, load/SLO work, SBOM, gallery/flow-player UI, or unrelated refactors? Are those explicitly deferred with the manual procedure defined?

security.instructions: Does the grain leak secrets (dumps contain workspace content — runbook requires encryption and operator-only access), bypass ledger guards silently (TRUNCATE bypass documented with no-dangling-refs reasoning, row-level takedown explicitly separate), or expose the drill beyond fixture databases (PG test gate refuses non-local/non-fixture targets)?
